scope: Experimental SIM-4B explicit rigid connectors, remote loads/supports, normalized connector force/moment resultants, the two-domain bolted L-bracket surrogate, and deterministic disconnected/underconstrained failure admission.

lanes.acceptance: The strict v2 contract admits explicit six-DOF connector/load/support identity and rejects unknown, unused, overlapping, or simultaneously loaded-and-supported connectors.
CalculiX reference- and rotation-node force resultants are normalized with exact connector and analysis-point identity; direct FACE constraints return null moments.

The two-domain bonded L-bracket with explicit bolt-group and eccentric-load connectors satisfies force and moment equilibrium within the fixture tolerances and produces finite displacement/stress fields.

The explicit domain-interaction graph and six-rigid-body-mode restraint rank reject an unsupported disconnected component and a connected bracket with one free rotation before CalculiX launch, preserve stable failure codes through the asynchronous provider lifecycle, and quarantine results.
An independent qualified engineer approves the connector formulation, sign conventions, benchmark geometry, tolerances, assumptions, and evidence for the exact reviewed commit.
